title: Product Designer

Hello Clever is building the next generation of payments and commerce infrastructure by turning every transaction into growth for merchants and clearer value for consumers. We’re an AI-powered fintech operating across 22+ markets, helping businesses move money in real time and convert payments into measurable outcomes like higher repeat rates, bigger baskets, and smarter customer engagement. Our platform combines local account-to-account rails, embedded rewards products, and powerful data intelligence through Clever AI so merchants can launch offers, optimize ROI, and scale faster through a single integration.

Unlock your potential with Hello Clever. We're seeking a thoughtful, hands-on, and customer-obsessed Product Designer to turn complex payments, rewards, data, and operational workflows into clear, trusted, and useful product experiences. - Base salary: $150,000 to $200,000 USD per year

We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. About Flint

The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.

Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school — every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.

Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

The Role

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.

Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. We’ll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.

How We Work



- We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we can’t keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.
- Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.
- We’re always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.
- Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. Mission to keep the world adventurous forever. While our vehicles redefine the road, our internal software redefines how a global company operates. We are building the "digital engine" intelligent, scalable platforms that allow us to move faster, smarter, and more sustainably.

We are seeking a Senior Product Designer to define the user experience for our AI-powered procurement platforms. You will design the interfaces that allow thousands of employees to interact with "agentic" workflows, turning complex supply chain logic into intuitive, guided digital experiences.


What You Will Do


● Product & Interface Strategy: Architect the user journey for complex, end-to-end internal applications. You will take ownership of the UX for major platform features, ensuring they are intuitive and resilient to user error.
● Frontend-Aligned Design: Design responsive, highly interactive, and accessible UIs. You will work closely with engineers to ensure designs account for complex global states and performance optimization.

● Design Tools: Mastery of Figma, including advanced prototyping and design system management.

● AI UX Frameworks: Experience designing for LLM interactions (handling latency, showing AI "thought processes," and providing feedback loops).
● Prototyping: Proficiency in tools like Protopie, Framer, or high-fidelity Figma prototyping to demonstrate multi-step agentic logic.
● Testing: Experience collaborating on usability testing and using feedback to iterate on complex enterprise tools. What We’re Looking For
● Experience: 5+ years of Product Design experience, specifically within B2B SaaS, Fintech, or complex internal enterprise tools.
● Architecture Focus: You possess the ability to simplify massive data sets and multi-step manual processes into clean, automated paths.
● Collaborative Mindset: You work seamlessly with engineers, understanding that the best designs are those that are safely and effectively deployed.

description:
About Your Role 👀

As the second Product Designer at Pogo, you'll help lead the product design and creative direction for our new consumer insights product, which allows brands/retailers to connect with millions of purchase-verified consumers. This platform will ultimately be used by some of the largest companies in the world.

Specifically, you will:



- Design core product experiences end-to-end, from early exploration through launch and iteration for our up-and-coming B2B platform and consumer app with 3 million users (and growing)
- Craft polished, delightful interfaces that build trust and showcase the power of our data and AI technology
- Sweat the details - layout, typography, spacing, color, motion, interactions
- Help define the product roadmap and lay the foundations for our design language, systems, and culture. 
- Find creative ways to ship high-quality work in a fast-paced, often ambiguous, startup environment
- Be 1 of 2 designers (for now), working cross-functionally with engineering and GTM

💎 We're looking for the best talent out there, so we're offering above-market salaries & equity.

About You 👩‍🚀



- Experience designing software products. 
- Bonus if you’ve done this at a startup, or have designed AI interactions before!
- Bonus if you have experience designing enterprise-grade products. 
- You design quickly and efficiently, using Figma to gain super powers and reach “escape velocity design”. When needed, you make near-term tradeoffs and take shortcuts - even though you have strong design vision and awareness of how to improve the product later. 
- You’re a design nerd at heart. You have a very high bar for design quality and strong opinions about what “great” looks like. You actively seek out the best-designed best products/designers, constantly collecting references from Twitter, Mobbin, and beyond. And you bring that level of rigor and polish into your own work.

- You’re relentless in pursuing the best solution - willing to explore, iterate, and even scrap a lot of your own work if it means creating a stronger product. 
- You’re a full-stack designer. You've designed experiences from scratch and know how to bring it to life working cross-functionally with product and engineering. 
- You have strong product intuition and have a knack for creating experiences that index on simplicity and clarity. At the same time, you're willing to re-consider your initial intuition as you get more user data. 

Why you might be excited about this opportunity 🙌



- Work on the design for an up-and-coming enterprise product. Our enterprise demand is growing, and we are in the early stages of building a product that will ultimately be used by some of the largest companies in the world. You’ll use qualitative interviews and direct customer feedback to shape product decisions and design solutions tailored to enterprise needs. 
- Design matters a lot to us.

Company Description Synter focuses on creating AI agents that drive sustainable business growth. The company builds intelligent, scalable solutions that help organizations optimize workflows, enhance customer experiences, and uncover new opportunities. Team members collaborate across disciplines to design products that are both technically robust and user-centered. Role Description This is a full-time remote role for a Product Designer at Synter. The Product Designer will collaborate with product managers, engineers, and other stakeholders to define problems, explore solutions, and design intuitive user experiences for AI-driven products. Day-to-day responsibilities include creating wireframes, user flows, and high-fidelity interfaces, conducting user research and usability testing, and translating insights into clear design decisions. - Experience with User Research and UX Research, including planning studies, synthesizing findings, and applying insights to design.

title: Product Designer, Amazon Music Product Design
description:
Description

As a Product Designer on the Amazon Music Core Experiences Design team, you will design voice-first and multimodal interactions that shape how customers experience music through spoken language. You'll work at the intersection of visual craft and conversational design — crafting TTS responses, anticipating how customers interpret single and multi-turn voice interactions, and ensuring spoken experiences pair seamlessly with on-screen content across Alexa-enabled devices.

Working alongside senior product designers, product managers, engineers, and researchers, you will support the design of voice interactions that feel natural, useful, and delightful. You'll use your knowledge of conversational UX and visual design to build, iterate, and refine solutions with guidance from your team. To succeed, you need a passion for language, empathy for how people listen and respond, strong visual sensibilities, and the curiosity to explore how voice and screen work together.

Key job responsibilities



-  Design voice interactions and TTS response flows that are clear, natural, and contextually appropriate for Amazon Music customers
-  Create conversational wireframes, sample dialog scripts, response mapping documents, and flow diagrams to communicate design intent
-  Iterate on single-turn and multi-turn voice interaction patterns, anticipating how customers will interpret and respond to spoken prompts
-  Collaborate with design, product, engineering, and research teams to incorporate customer feedback, technical constraints, and usability findings into designs
-  Leverage existing templates and design systems to produce high-fidelity mockups for multimodal voice+screen experiences
-  Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure voice responses align with broader platform patterns
-  Present design work to partners and stakeholders for review and feedback
-  Contribute to language model training data and sample dialog interactions under guidance from senior designers

A day in the life

You'll start your day reviewing how a new TTS response sounds and reads on an Echo Show — does it feel rushed? Is the information hierarchy right when paired with the visual card? You'll sketch out a multi-turn flow for a new music request pattern, thinking through what happens when a customer says "no, not that one." You'll pair with your PM to walk through edge cases, sync with an engineer on what's technically feasible for response latency, and bring your work to a design crit where the team helps you refine the conversational cadence. You'll end the day documenting your iteration in Figma and noting open questions for research.

title: Product Designer
description:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About The Role

title: Product Designer
description:
Compensation: $160k–190k base + meaningful equity

About Flint

The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.

Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school — every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.

Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

The Role

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.

Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. We’ll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.

How We Work



- We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we can’t keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.
- Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.
- We’re always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.
- Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. We'd rather build from real user feedback and a range of perspectives than from any one person's classroom experience. Our close connection with teachers, students, and admins helps us quickly understand what's working and what isn't.

Description

As a Product Designer on the Amazon Music Core Experiences Design team, you will design voice-first and multimodal interactions that shape how customers experience music through spoken language. You'll work at the intersection of visual craft and conversational design — crafting TTS responses, anticipating how customers interpret single and multi-turn voice interactions, and ensuring spoken experiences pair seamlessly with on-screen content across Alexa-enabled devices.

Working alongside senior product designers, product managers, engineers, and researchers, you will support the design of voice interactions that feel natural, useful, and delightful. You'll use your knowledge of conversational UX and visual design to build, iterate, and refine solutions with guidance from your team. To succeed, you need a passion for language, empathy for how people listen and respond, strong visual sensibilities, and the curiosity to explore how voice and screen work together.

Key job responsibilities



-  Design voice interactions and TTS response flows that are clear, natural, and contextually appropriate for Amazon Music customers
-  Create conversational wireframes, sample dialog scripts, response mapping documents, and flow diagrams to communicate design intent
-  Iterate on single-turn and multi-turn voice interaction patterns, anticipating how customers will interpret and respond to spoken prompts
-  Collaborate with design, product, engineering, and research teams to incorporate customer feedback, technical constraints, and usability findings into designs
-  Leverage existing templates and design systems to produce high-fidelity mockups for multimodal voice+screen experiences
-  Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure voice responses align with broader platform patterns
-  Present design work to partners and stakeholders for review and feedback
-  Contribute to language model training data and sample dialog interactions under guidance from senior designers

A day in the life

You'll start your day reviewing how a new TTS response sounds and reads on an Echo Show — does it feel rushed? Is the information hierarchy right when paired with the visual card? You'll sketch out a multi-turn flow for a new music request pattern, thinking through what happens when a customer says "no, not that one." You'll pair with your PM to walk through edge cases, sync with an engineer on what's technically feasible for response latency, and bring your work to a design crit where the team helps you refine the conversational cadence. You'll end the day documenting your iteration in Figma and noting open questions for research.

Amazon Music is an immersive audio entertainment service that deepens connections between fans, artists, and creators. title: Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

What you'll do



- Design and build products from concept through launch.
- Work closely with design and engineering on new features and launches.
- You care about the details—typography, layout, motion, responsiveness, loading states, and performance—that make an experience great.
- Contribute visual assets for marketing.
- Prototype ideas quickly using Figma, Claude, Cursor, and whatever tools helps move the work forward.

You might be a fit if



- You have 2–5 years of experience designing and building for the web.
- You move fluidly across the full design process, from early concept through final production.
- You have an instinct for the details that make interfaces feel considered: type, spacing, motion, and how they all work together.
- You know enough HTML and CSS to work effectively with engineers—or to build parts of the experience yourself.
- You're comfortable using tools like Claude

Reducto is the agentic document platform for leading AI teams who demand enterprise performance at scale. We provide a comprehensive toolkit for working with documents the way a human would, combining custom in-house and leading frontier models to power efficient and accurate document workflows.

We’ve grown rapidly, increasing revenue 8x year over year and partnering with hundreds of companies, from leading AI teams like Harvey, Vanta, and Scale, to enterprise customers across FAANG and top trading firms.

Reducto has raised over $100M from world-class investors including a16z, Benchmark, and First Round Capital.

The Opportunity

As an early member of our product design team you’ll shape the foundation of how users interact with our product—from core workflows to visual language. You’ll work directly with our CEO, engineers, and customers to design entirely new experiences. We don’t have PMs— so you’ll own design end-to-end: user research, UX flows, wireframes, high-fidelity mocks, and design systems.

We Would Love To Meet You If



- You are your own worst critic. You have a high bar for quality and don’t rest until the job is done right—no settling for 90%. We want someone who ships fast, with high agency, and who doesn't just voice problems but actively jumps in to fix them.
- You’ve shipped complex products before for 2+ years, ideally for engineers, researchers, or ops-heavy teams.
- You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity and defining structure where none exists.
- You move fast, but also care deeply about polish and craft.

The Core Work Will Include



- Lead design end-to-end for Reducto, owning everything from defining a world-class brand to shipping beautiful experiences that users love.
- Develop brand new products and user workflows.
- Build and own our design system, brand, and how we present ourselves to the world.
- Obsess over the small details, driving a culture that highly values design.

Bonus Points If You



- Have prior experience founding a company or building products at early stages
- Are ambitious and driven, and care a lot about doing great work with great people
- Keep up with the latest developments in ML/AI

Benefits



- Unlimited PTO: We believe great work requires recharging.
- Lunch: Receive a free lunch to eat with your teammates daily at the office
- Reimbursed Transportation: Provide us with your receipts and we’ll take care of the costs
- Insurance: Generous health insurance covering medical, dental, and vision.
- Health and Wellness Budget: We provide up to $150/mo reimbursement for health and wellness spending, such as gym memberships, fitness classes, or similar.
- Parental Leave: Work with us to build a leave schedule that works for you and your family

This is an in person role at our office in SF. We’re an early stage company which means that the role requires working hard and moving quickly. Please only apply if that excites you.

title: Brand Designer, Strategic Initiatives - Instagram Brand Studio
description:
Instagram Brand Studio shapes how Instagram expresses itself to the world — through brand systems, visual identity, campaign design, and creative tools that reach billions of people.As Brand Designer, you will bring Instagram's brand to life through visual design, interaction, and immersive storytelling. You will define iconic interactive brand experiences for in-app moments and marketing activations. You'll partner closely with product design, marketing, creative, and engineering teams to define how our brand behaves, responds, and communicates in dynamic contexts.You're equal parts systems thinker and hands-on maker. You'll work across the spectrum — from fast, rough motion studies to polished, production-ready deliverables — and you'll champion craft while making smart trade-offs at scale. title: Product Designer
description:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About The Role

Imagine yourself in the 1970s or 80s thinking through how computing should look and feel for people who had never seen one before. That's what we're trying to do at Notion — make software that feels timeless, with the craftsmanship of German cameras, playfulness of Japanese toys, and mass appeal of Coca-Cola. We have no end of fascinating challenges that can only be solved by someone with innate product & UX sense, technical aptitude, great taste, and impeccable craft.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve



- Design product concepts that balance vision, craft, speed, and business potential.
- Craft every detail of new product features, from idea to UX to pixel-perfect execution.
- Run projects end to end with engineers to drive your vision to the ship line.
- Partner closely with our Customer Experience, Sales, and Customer Success teams to understand what each of our diverse user segments need, want, and love about Notion. Use this data and acquired intuition to prioritize, plan, and scope our product roadmap.
- Work with Marketing to devise new ways to tell great stories throughout the user lifecycle, and across our site, product, help guides and other channels.
- Create new patterns that are intuitive, practical, and convergent. Evolve our design system intentionally as we scale.

Skills You'll Need To Bring



- You have well-rounded skills and experience to run projects independently end to end. 5+ years of working experience.
- You seek to understand the needs of customers then explore and advocate for the strongest user experiences to solve their problems
- You enjoy untangling vague conceptual problems and have a sharp intuition for the most accessible mental models and flows, so users can immediately start gaining value out of the product.
- You create clear, intuitive, and visually appealing human interfaces

title: Product Designer I
description:
ICON is hiring a UX professional to own the user experience for a core product area within BuildOS - our software platform used by architects, builders, and construction operators. In this role, you will lead end-to-end UX work for tools that connect users to ICON's construction technology, from discovery research through design handoff. You will run customer interviews, map complex workflows, build prototypes, test them with real users, and write specs that engineering can build from. You will work alongside engineers, product leadership, and internal and external customers to shape what gets built and why. This role is based at ICON's Austin, TX office and reports to the Director of Product.


RESPONSIBILITIES:
Discovery and Research: Run regular interviews with architects, engineers, and builders to learn their workflows, pain points, and unmet needs. Document assumptions, evidence gaps, and research priorities for your product area. Turn findings into clear insights that shape the roadmap.
Workflow Mapping and UX Design: Map user workflows and edge cases for complex, multi-step construction and design processes. Design for a range of users, from technical specialists to first-time operators with different levels of software fluency. Define data needs, integration points, and error states.
Wireframes and Prototypes: Create wireframes, interaction flows, and interactive prototypes in Figma or a similar tool. Deliver designs that are functional, polished, and clear.
Prototyping and Usability Testing: Build and test prototypes with target users on a regular cadence. Run lightweight usability tests and update designs based on real feedback. Check designs with engineering for technical feasibility before handoff.
Handoff and Engineering Collaboration: Deliver developer-ready specs with annotated designs, acceptance criteria, and interaction details. Work two or more sprints ahead of engineering so teams always have clear, well-defined work to pick up.
Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate daily with engineers, product leadership, and cross-functional partners. Present design choices to engineers, leaders, and customers in plain terms.
Strategic Alignment: Connect your design work to company-wide Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) so the user experience moves bigger goals forward.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

- 3+ in UX design, product design, or a similar role.
- A portfolio showing end-to-end design work — research through shipped product, not visual design alone.
- Experience running user interviews and turning qualitative research into design decisions.
- Strong fluency with Figma or a similar tool for wireframing, prototyping, and design systems.
- Experience designing for workflows with real constraints, not only consumer apps.
- Clear communication skills. You can explain design choices to engineers, leaders, and customers.
- Comfort working through ambiguity. You can define the problem, not just solve a defined one.

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. What Lumion does
Lumion is the all-in-one operating system for trade and technical schools. We power the entire institution: AI-driven lead generation and conversion, enrollment, financial aid, student lifecycle management, and tuition payments. Most schools are still stitching together five or six disconnected tools to do what our platform handles.


America has a massive skilled trades shortage and the schools that train electricians, welders, and nurses are the bottleneck. We're backed by TTV Capital and Tusk Venture Partners.
Why this role matters


You would be Lumion's first dedicated product designer. Until now, design has been done by the founders, product managers, and engineers. That carried us a long way, and it is no longer enough.


Our engineers build with AI-native workflows, so the constraint on the product is no longer how fast we can write code. It is how fast we can figure out exactly what to build and make it excellent. That is design work, and right now it is our bottleneck.


The people who use our platform are admissions directors, school owners, and finance staff who live in it all day, and students making one of the bigger financial decisions of their lives. Most software in this industry was built a decade ago and looks like it. You get to set the bar for what great looks like in this market.


The work
You will own design across the entire platform.


Product design end to end. You take features from PRD to shipped: user flows, interaction design, high-fidelity UI, and specs engineers can build from without guessing. You will work directly with the CEO and CTO in design sessions and own the outcome.


Prototypes. Before engineering commits to a build, we want a working prototype in front of real schools. You will produce clickable, testable prototypes fast and use what you learn to sharpen the spec before a line of production code gets written.


The design system. The platform spans lead management, enrollment, messaging, scheduling, payments, and reporting, and it grew fast. You will build the component library and interaction patterns that make it feel like one product, and that let engineers ship good UI without a designer in the room.


AI interfaces. Schools use Lumion to configure and supervise AI agents that text, email, and call prospective students. Designing how a non-technical admissions director sets up an agent, reviews its conversations, and learns to trust it is new territory with little prior art. You will define those patterns.


Student surfaces. Enrollment applications, document signing, and tuition payments, mostly on a phone. These flows handle real money and real decisions, and they have to be effortless.

title: Staff Product Designer
description:
Staff Product Designer


Remote (US) · Full-time
Lead product design for VA.gov services that help Veterans get the benefits and care they have earned. Remote across the United States.


About the role
Selara is hiring a Staff Product Designer to work on VA.gov, the digital front door for the Department of Veterans Affairs. The services you design reach millions of Veterans who use VA.gov to apply for benefits, manage their health care, and track their claims. Good design here is not decoration. It is the difference between a Veteran finishing an application and giving up on it.
This is a staff level role. You will ship product design on a cross-functional team and raise the design bar well beyond your own work.


What you'll do

- Own product design for VA.gov experiences end to end, from discovery and research through shipped, measured outcomes
- Plan and run research with Veterans and VA staff, then turn findings into decisions the whole team can act on
- Design within the VA Design System and contribute improvements back to it, so every experience stays consistent with the rest of VA.gov
- Design form-heavy, high-stakes flows in plain language that people can complete under stress
- Treat accessibility as a first-class design constraint and deliver work that meets WCAG 2.1 AA and Section 508 from the first draft, not as a cleanup pass
- Work shoulder to shoulder with engineers, iterating in staging and reviewing built work against design intent
- Set design standards, mentor designers and teammates in user-centered practice, and represent design in program-level reviews


What we're looking for

- Significant product design experience, typically eight or more years across research, interaction design, visual design, and content design
- A portfolio of shipped, complex services, ideally forms, eligibility flows, or other transactional experiences rather than marketing surfaces
- Hands-on research skill, including usability testing, synthesis, and the judgment to pick lightweight methods that fit the moment
- Deep working knowledge of accessible design practice and experience shipping to WCAG and Section 508 standards
- Fluency working inside a mature design system and the judgment to know when to extend it
- Strong facilitation, writing, and mentoring skills in a remote, distributed team
- The ability to influence product direction through partnership rather than authority


Nice to have

- Experience designing for VA.gov, another federal agency, or regulated industries like health care
- Familiarity with the US Web Design System or the VA Design System
- Experience with government design review cycles such as design intent and staging reviews
- Comfort reading and lightly prototyping in HTML and CSS


Location and eligibility
This role is fully remote within the United States. Work on VA.gov requires the ability to obtain and maintain a federal Public Trust suitability determination, which includes a background investigation.

What We Offer

- Competitive salary and equity package

description:
Visual Brand & Marketing Designer (New York)
Ruca — US Studio
Contract-to-Hire / Remote (NYC based)

About Ruca
Ruca is a member-owned global creative cooperative with a boutique soul. We partner with companies seeking proven experience, speed, and scale to launch recognizable brands, products, and businesses. We bring strategy-led services, amplified by the latest technologies, to every engagement. 
Unlike traditional design agencies, we also invest in founders, incubate our own products, and share in collective success with our members through equity and profit-sharing. 
We’re building something different, and we want people who want to build with us.

The Role
We’re looking for a strong, AI-Native visual designer with up to seven years of experience to join Ruca's US Studio on a 3-month, full-time contract, with the goal of converting to a permanent member of our product design team. This contract is built to convert: if you're the right fit, full-time employment follows at the 3-month mark. As a member of our US Local Studio, you will work on client work, internal brands, and venture projects across a diverse range of engagements from visual identity systems to pitch decks to social campaigns. You will work alongside a global community of experienced creatives including our two other Local Studios in Bogota and Manila. 
This is a role for someone who is already using AI tools fluently in their creative process, has a sharp eye for craft, and is ready to grow inside a cooperative that rewards initiative and shares its success.
While we work remotely, we believe the best creative culture is built in person. US Studio members gather regularly with co-founders in Los Angeles, Chicago, and New York. Candidates should be comfortable making their way to one of these cities on a monthly basis.

Core Responsibilities
A strong design foundation is a must. An AI-native practice is critical. We expect you to have a solid creative craft and know how to use AI tools to amplify it through standard instruments in your design process, such as prototypes, workflow automations, copy, and generative images and videos.



- Use AI-assisted tools (workflow automation, ideation, rapid prototyping) to accelerate concept development and expand creative range

title: Principal Product Designer
description:
About Agora Intelligence (d.b.a. Tilt)
Agora Intelligence is building the audited methodology layer agents call before touching portfolios. Our product, Tilt, is GitHub for rules-based investment methodologies: an open platform and marketplace where investment strategies are created, tested, audited, and distributed — by humans and AI agents alike. As AI agents begin managing real portfolios, they need a trusted source of verified investment logic before they can act. Tilt is that source.
We operate across two connected surfaces: InvestOS, an open standard that lets any brokerage or platform plug verified methodology into its own AI experience; and Tilt, the reference implementation of InvestOS. Tilt is an agentic harness where investors, portfolio managers, and creators can author, remix, and publish strategies. We're a small, senior team (from BlackRock, Bloomberg, BGI, and Quant Funds) backed by Portage Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Cumberland Investments (and more), working with major brokerages and financial data providers.


What We're Building
InvestOS — an open standard for rules-based methodologies and its reference implementation.
We believe any idea — a theme, a trend, a thesis — can be turned into an investable view. On Tilt, anyone can express a view as a rules-based basket of assets in seconds, backed by evidence and scored against what actually happens. Whether you're modeling a thematic strategy, tracking an emerging technology, or capturing the public-market footprint of a private company, what used to take an index committee months now takes an API call — 100× faster, at a fraction of the cost. We also transform views found on the open web, into rules-based strategies. This lets us measure the performance of any opinion or prediction about the future. The unit is a tilt: a creator-authored view of the world.


The bigger bet: as AI agents take on more of investing, they'll need an open, trusted standard for how investment views are expressed, verified, and combined. When anyone can generate a strategy in seconds, the strategies aren't the asset. The system that versions, tests, and grades them is. We're building that standard — and the platform where those views are made. We’re also building the learning loops for when views resolve against reality, as measured by markets.


Who We Are
We're a team of ~25 senior-to-principal engineers, designers and AI/ML researchers. More than half the team are former founders. We move fast, challenge assumptions, and believe AI should fundamentally change how financial products are built. We have no management hierarchy and work remotely with 4 one-week hackathons per year. “Full stack” to us means you own a slice of the product, including its roadmap and go-to-market.

title: Studio Designer
description:
Studio Designer
You’re the person who makes sure beautiful ideas leave the building flawlessly.
You love the details, file names, specs, color profiles, bleeds, versions, all of it. When something goes to a media partner or print vendor, you want it buttoned-up, on spec, and on time.
At Zimmerman Agency, we’re looking for a Studio Designer with strong technical and production design skills to be a key part of our creative process.
What you’ll do

- Prepare and finalize production-ready files for print, OOH, digital, and social
- Handle pre-press tasks: setting up bleeds, crops, color profiles, imposition needs, and printer requirements
- Version, resize, and adapt existing designs across multiple formats and specs
- Ensure all deliverables meet technical requirements for print shops, media partners, and digital platforms
- Maintain organized file structures, naming conventions, and version control
- Collaborate closely with the design and creative teams to ensure work is accurate, consistent, and on-brand
- Perform quality control checks on files before they go out the door
- Problem-solve with vendors and internal teams when specs change or issues arise
What you bring

- Proven technical design / production design experience (agency or in-house studio experience a plus)
- Strong abilities in Adobe Creative Cloud (InDesign, Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat for pre-press checks)
- Solid understanding of:
- Pre-press and print production (CMYK vs RGB, resolution, bleeds, safety, etc.)
- Digital file prep for web and social (sizes, formats, compression, platform specs)
- Detail-obsessed and highly organized, you take pride in clean files and tight workflows
- Comfortable working with templates, guidelines, and brand systems
- Accountable and reliable, deadlines matter and you don’t let things slip
- Strong communicator who can work with designers, project managers, and vendors to get files right
- Positive, collaborative attitude
Why you’ll love working here

- You’ll be central to getting the work out into the world, your fingerprints will be on everything
- A tight, collaborative creative team that values the studio role (we know nothing ships without you)
- A fun, travel-focused agency environment with varied clients and formats
- On-site in Tallahassee, FL, working shoulder-to-shoulder with designers and creatives
- A stable role with room to grow your skills in both print and digital production

description:
🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot!

Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. We're building live commerce at a scale that's never been done in the West, and there's no playbook to copy. The people here are shaping how an entirely new industry develops.

As a remote co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the US, UK, Ireland, Poland, Germany, and Australia. We move fast, stay close to our users, and focus on the work that drives the most impact.

We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. Check out the latest Whatnot updates on our news and engineering blogs and join us as we enable anyone to turn their passion into a business and bring people together through commerce.

💻 Role

We’re looking for a Product Designer to join our Payments team—someone who’s passionate about designing seamless, trustworthy money experiences for live commerce at massive scale. In this role, you’ll shape the checkout, payout, wallet, and incentive experiences that power every dollar moving through Whatnot, from the moment a buyer wins or buys in a live show to the moment a seller understands, receives, and manages their earnings.

You’ll partner closely with product managers, engineers, data scientists, and finance, compliance, and risk partners to build experiences that balance speed, trust, and operational correctness. This could include designing one-tap and multi-step payment flows, seller-facing pending payment and payout experiences, wallet and stored-value systems, or recovery paths for failed payments, disputes, and chargebacks.

What You’ll Do



- Design payment and value experiences across checkout, payouts, wallet, refunds, credits, coupons, gift cards, and emerging balance products on web and mobile.
- Translate payment infrastructure, compliance, tax, and financial integrity requirements into intuitive product experiences.
- Design both happy paths and recovery flows: failed payments, pending states, payment method switching, seller visibility, and resolution.
- Create wireframes, prototypes, and polished product experiences for ambiguous, high-stakes money movement problems.
- Help unify fragmented payment experiences across live, marketplace, tips, offers, and other purchase surfaces.
- Use data, research, and experimentation to improve conversion, reduce payment friction, and increase buyer and seller confidence.
- Contribute to the design system while advocating for accessibility, inclusivity, and scalable global patterns.
- Design for live shopping constraints, where speed, clarity, and trust matter across auctions, flash sales, subscriptions, and other high-throughput moments.

description:
About A1
There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks that are not AI-native. Our mission is to build a proactive smart assistant for everyday users to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal prompting.
Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. The system must handle multi-step reasoning, interact with external tools, and remain reliable despite non-deterministic model behavior. Our objective is to help users complete tasks daily enjoyable with over ~90%* reduced time.
Role
Design how people use AI in real product workflows. This role focuses on building HCI interfaces where users can understand, guide, correct, and stay in control of AI systems that reason and act across multiple steps.
Current UX patterns are not enough for proactive AI products. You will help define new interaction models for how users work with AI, review progress, recover from mistakes, and build trust in the system.

- Design end-to-end user experiences for AI product surfaces, from concept to shipped product.
- Create interaction patterns for human-AI workflows, including prompting, review, confirmation, correction, handoff, and recovery.
- Design interfaces that help users understand what the AI is doing, what it knows, what it is unsure about, and what will happen next.
- Turn complex, multi-step AI capabilities into flows that are clear, controllable, and usable in everyday contexts.
- Work closely with product, engineering, and ML teams to define problems, test ideas, and ship quickly.
- Produce wireframes, flows, prototypes, and high-fidelity designs for web and mobile.
- Run lightweight user research and usability tests to identify friction, trust issues, and failure points.
- Help define reusable HCI design patterns as the product and design system mature.
What You Will Need

- Experience as a product designer or UX designer, with a portfolio across web or mobile products.
- Strong skills in interaction design, information hierarchy, and prototyping.
- Proficiency in Figma and fast iteration workflows.
- Ability to simplify complex systems and turn unclear product behavior into clear user experiences.
- Experience working closely with product managers and engineers in fast-moving teams.
- Comfort working with ambiguity and shaping solutions before requirements are fully defined.
- Good judgment on usability, edge cases, and failure handling.
- Clear thinking about trust, control, feedback, and transparency in AI-driven experiences.
How We Work
The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. We are executing a complex Figma design system migration—moving a large, interconnected Figma environment from one enterprise account to another. The work involves shared libraries, component hierarchies, and a token architecture managed through Token Studio. 
We are seeking a Figma specialist with deep design systems expertise to lead this effort. You will be embedded with our design team, working hands-on through every phase of the migration. - Ensure the token architecture supports a scalable, independent design system
 Migration Execution

- Coordinate with organizational admins for team-level transfers to the new enterprise account
- Execute the migration in a sequenced manner that minimizes disruption to active design work
- Perform full QA on the migrated environment prior to handoff, ensuring no broken references, missing libraries, or disconnected tokens
 
What You Bring Required

title: Visual Design Apprentice
description:
Visual Design Apprentice


The Short Version
You make things beautiful. Not “clean and modern” beautiful. Stop-scrolling, zoom-in, who-made-this beautiful. You'll design the visual identity systems, product interfaces, and brand assets for ventures that don't exist yet.


What Liminal Is
A Founders' Studio. We co-build with repeat founders, many of them unicorn founders, providing build expertise, capital, and unfair access from founding to Series B. We call ourselves a Founders' Studio because “venture studio” undersells what we do and oversells what most of them deliver.


What This Role Actually Is
Dirty secret in design hiring: the Venn of great visual and great UX designers barely overlaps. We hire for the visual circle. Emphatically.


You build the visual layer for a venture: identity, interfaces, decks, assets. You turn positioning into something a founder looks at and says "that's us." You sweat what others don't see. Optical alignment. The weight of whitespace. Why one shade of blue reads "trustworthy fintech" and the one three hex values over reads "dental office."


The Work

- Visual identity and brand systems. Translate brand strategy into complete visual identities: typography, color, layout grids, iconography, the overall look and feel that makes a venture cohesive across every touchpoint.
- Product and digital surfaces. Design clean, visually engaging UI for early-stage products: landing pages, dashboards, onboarding flows, marketing pages. You own the high-fidelity output and work directly with engineering so what ships looks like what you designed.
- Brand assets at scale. Decks, social content, one-pagers, investor materials, event collateral. Often the first thing the outside world sees. They need to be flawless.
- Design system stewardship. Build and maintain coherent design languages that hold up as the venture grows, so the hundredth asset looks as considered as the first.


Who You Are

- Exceptional visual craft. A portfolio that makes us lean in. Strong command of typography, color theory, composition, and layout across brand and digital surfaces. You know the difference between beautiful and merely pretty. You can explain why, in terms that aren't just vibes.
- Exquisite taste. Omnivorous and opinionated. You have feelings about restaurant menus, movie title sequences, transit signage, and the packaging on your toothpaste. Your taste is informed by what you've consumed across design, art, architecture, fashion, and culture. Not just what Dribbble served you last week.
- Tool fluency. Figma and Adobe Creative Suite are second nature. You work fast, iterate without preciousness, and produce high-fidelity output that doesn't need a translator between you and engineering.
- Comfort with ambiguity. No brand guides. No existing design systems. No “make it like the last one.” A founder, a blank page, and a company that needs to look like it was inevitable. That should thrill you.
- Contrarian streak. Independent thinker. Arg

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
Position Overview
We're building Leap Crew, an agentic platform for the trades, and it's the biggest product bet at Leap. The idea: the software captures the work as it happens, AI agents absorb the routine data-entry and busywork contractors pay for with their time today, and the contractor stays in control the whole way. Done right, it hands a roofer or a window installer back hours of their week.
The design canvas here is wide open. Leap Crew has no dedicated designer yet, which means its interaction model is still largely yours to define. How do you make an AI agent something a contractor actually trusts with their business? What does it show when it's unsure? What happens when it's wrong in front of a homeowner? Those questions don't have textbook answers yet. We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to help write them.
The people you design for run real businesses in demanding conditions. A rep closing a $30,000 job at a kitchen table. An installer in a truck with bad signal. An owner deciding whether to trust a number the software just generated. Get the design right and you move their close rate, their cash flow, and how confidently they grow. Get it wrong and they feel it fast. AI raises the stakes on both sides: done well it's a real advantage for the contractor, done carelessly it erodes trust that took years to earn.
As the senior designer on Leap Crew, you'll own its design end to end. You'll work on a senior team where product and engineering operate as one, and you'll be the design voice in the room from the first sketch.
Within your first year, the first cohort of contractors should be live on Leap Crew and measurably spending less of their day on data entry, with an agentic interaction model the rest of the team designs against. You'll have killed some directions on evidence. When the teams closest to contractors, in CS, Sales, and Marketing, hit a hard product problem, they'll come to you for a designer's take on it.
What You’ll Own

- The end-to-end design vision for the platform, including the north-star artifacts (experience principles, concept designs, future-state flows) that give the team a shared target
- The agentic experience itself, the heart of this role: how the system proposes work, how a contractor reviews and overrides it, its error and low-confidence states, and how control stays with the human even as the agent does more
- A continuous research practice with ongoing relationships with the contractors piloting the platform, well beyond a formal session cadence
- The quality conscience for the experience: contractor-ready set before development, defended at release, and post-launch contractor signal treated as a leading indicator rather than a lagging report
- The design system for a new product: proposing the components and patterns the rest of the team will build on
- Design strategy that shapes what the team builds next, not just how it looks
- Raising the craft bar of the designers around you: specific critique

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About Nuvo

Nuvo is building the infrastructure that powers trade in the physical goods economy.

Every part of modern life depends on physical goods: the food we eat, the fabric we wear, the steel and concrete that shape our cities. Behind it all are 50 million businesses trading $100 trillion each year.

Consider how housing gets built. One company cuts down trees, another turns the wood into building materials, another sells the product wholesale, and a contractor uses them to build homes. Each step is a business trading with another to turn raw materials into finished goods.

Most of these businesses still operate through offline networks, held together by fragmented systems, manual processes, and institutional memory. When trade is slow, costly, or error-prone, the effects cascade — resources get misallocated, businesses can’t grow, and consumers face higher costs and fewer choices.

Nuvo builds technology that makes trade fast, automated, and intelligent. More than 75,000 businesses already use our platform, and we’re backed by $45M from Sequoia, Spark, Founders Fund, and Index as we build the operating system for global commerce.

The Role

Design at Nuvo sits at the center of how our platform works and feels. Our products span identity, risk, payments, AI, and more, all built on top of the connectivity between businesses on our platform. As a Senior Product Designer, you’ll shape how this system comes to life for thousands of businesses, defining how complex operations become simple, intuitive, and powerful.

You’ll operate with deep ownership, collaborating closely with engineering, product, and customer teams. You’ll help define the next generation of experiences that make Nuvo increasingly compelling across new industries and use cases.

- Drive design for major product areas that serve thousands of businesses
- Partner with engineers to build progressively and deliver high-quality results at speed
- Develop and scale our design language and system across surfaces and products
- Engage with customers to uncover insights and design from first principles
- Help define the design team’s culture, identity, and creative standards

- You collaborate with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders, making thoughtful trade-offs, relaying context, and being a clear voice of the customer
- Have 5+ years in industry shipping high-impact products to solve complex problems

Expected Compensation Range $180,000-$250,000

title: Product Designer
description:
Location: Austin, TX (Hybrid on-site, with up to 30% travel)

Requirement: U.S. citizenship with ability to obtain security clearance

About NODA

NODA is a veteran-owned, venture-backed technology company that is transforming how unmanned systems collaborate in complex, mission-critical environments. We are developing next-generation solutions that enable the autonomous orchestration of heterogeneous unmanned systems across air, sea, land, and space with vital applications in the defense, intelligence, and commercial sectors.

We are building a comprehensive tactical military interface platform that serves as the command center for mission-critical operations. Our product designers craft experiences that enable operators to confidently manage complex data from unmanned systems and make split-second decisions in real-time operational environments.

Joining NODA means working on meaningful technology that pushes the boundaries of autonomy alongside a team that thrives on innovation, rapid iteration, and collaboration.

The Role

We are seeking a Senior to Lead Product Designer to drive the design vision and execution for our tactical military interface platform. This role requires a designer who can translate complex operational requirements into intuitive, mission-critical interfaces while establishing design excellence across the product. You'll work at the intersection of user needs, technical constraints, and business objectives to create experiences that empower military operators in high-stakes environments. This position offers the opportunity to grow into a design leadership role as our team and product expand.

Key Responsibilities



- Lead end-to-end product design for core features including battle management, asset tracking, operational planning, and event monitoring interfaces
- Collaborate with product managers, engineers, and military stakeholders to define product requirements and translate them into elegant design solutions
- Create detailed design specifications including interaction patterns, component states, precise measurements, and visual specifications for engineering implementation
- Conduct user research with military operators and stakeholders to understand workflows, pain points, and operational requirements in tactical environments
- Design and prototype complex interfaces for real-time data visualization, tactical mapping, multi-asset coordination, and mission planning
- Establish and maintain design patterns and conventions that ensure consistency across the platform while establishing design system practices
- Present design concepts and rationale to stakeholders including CEO, product leadership, engineering teams and leadership, and customer representatives
- Iterate rapidly based on user feedback, technical constraints, and evolving operational requirements
- Mentor junior designers and contribute to building a culture of design excellence at NODA
- Balance innovation with practical constraints of defense sector

- Familiarity with AI-assisted design tooling (Figma MCP, generative workflows, agentic prototyping) is a strong plus

-  You run your own research rather than waiting for it to be handed to you. 
-  Excellent cross-functional communication — you can partner closely with Engineering and hold a position under scrutiny. 
-  Deep fluency in Figma and modern prototyping workflows.

description:
Remote · 3 to 4 week project · Start immediately


About ProMom
ProMom is an AI companion for the whole motherhood journey, from trying to conceive through pregnancy and postpartum. One app instead of six, with guidance shaped by a Medical Advisory Team of OB-GYNs and pediatricians. We are private by design, we do not sell user data, and we are ad free.


We are a small, fast team. Our users are often overwhelmed, anxious, and exhausted. Everything we build has to feel calm.


The project
We are mid-way through a full redesign of the app. Two in-house UX designers are building in Figma right now, and they are blocked on brand decisions. We need a brand designer to make those decisions and hand them a system they can build with immediately.


This is not a brand guide that gets delivered at the end and filed away. Your work goes straight into a live product build, week by week.


What you will deliver

- Color palette. A brand palette for marketing, plus an extended app color system that can express user stage (trying to conceive, pregnancy, postpartum) and functional states.
- Typography. Type direction for brand and app. Our current type reads techy. We want calm, human, and legible when someone is tired.
- Logo and app icon. A light refresh of the existing logo, evolution not redesign, plus the lockups we need. And a new App Store icon that reads at 60px on a home screen, our most-seen brand asset.
- Illustration style and brand design elements. The visual language that carries across app and marketing.
- Iconography direction. You set the style and our in-house UX team builds the library against it. If the icons only need a restyle, that is a direction-and-review job. If they need a full redesign, we will decide together who is best placed to build them.
- Brand style guide. Documented in Figma with our UX team as we go, so brand and app stay one system.
Not in scope: photography, marketing templates, website design.


How we work together
You lead brand direction and design judgment. Our two UX designers execute at scale. That means a kickoff together, a weekly working session, and shared Figma access so they can build with your work in real time rather than waiting.


Sequence matters. Color and typography come first because the app build is blocked on them. Illustration and icon direction follow immediately after, not at the end, because our designers are producing those assets now.


What we need from you
Must have

- Strong color, typography, and systems thinking. You have built a color and type system that shipped inside a real product, not just a logo and a moodboard.
- Experience across both brand and product design. You can hand a UX team something they can actually build with.
- Real availability. This is the single biggest factor for us. Roughly 12 to 20 hours a week for the next 3 to 4 weeks, starting now. If you are fitting this around a full-time job, it is probably not a fit.

Artemis Security is hiring a Product Designer to shape how security teams actually use our platform. In cybersecurity, most tools are built by engineers for engineers, and it shows - dense UIs, buried workflows, and dashboards no one actually looks at. We're building something different: a platform that security teams reach for because it's genuinely well-designed, not just powerful.

You'll own the end-to-end product experience across the Artemis platform, from the earliest concept sketches through pixel-perfect execution. title: SENIOR PRODUCT DESIGNER
description:
01 The Role

DESIGN

THE

FUTURE

of sport.

You won't be making another checkout flow. You'll be rethinking what it means to buy the shoe you trained in — the intersection of performance data, personal expression, and the athlete's relationship with Nike Direct.

"We believe if you have a body, you are an athlete. Design for that."

This role sits at the center of Nike's digital direct-to-consumer strategy — the place where brand becomes product, and product becomes a relationship.

02 What You'll Do

Craft & Scope

OWN THE

Whole

CANVAS.

Lead end-to-end design across Nike.com's commerce experience — from discovery to post-purchase. You'll shape information architecture, interaction systems, and visual execution with equal care.

Focus Area Nike Direct Digital Commerce (Nike.com)

Deliverables Research synthesis, flows, prototypes, shipped product

Collaboration PM, Engineering, Brand, Data Science, Merchandising

Tools Figma, Protopie, Looker, custom Nike design system

You won't be a UI merchant. You'll be the advocate for the athlete's experience — in the room with engineering when tradeoffs get made, and at the table when strategy gets set.

We don't design features. We design moments of belief — the instant someone puts the shoe in the bag.

03 The Culture

WIN AS

A TEAM.

Nike's culture is about being on the offense always. You'll work alongside designers who are also athletes, researchers who compete, and engineers who coach youth leagues on weekends.

Nike Direct Design is a creative team that ships. We have a bias for action, a reverence for craft, and a standing weekly critique that gets heated in the best way.

Failure is part of the playbook — because innovation depends on risk. What matters is that you own it and come back faster.

04 Who You Are

What moves you

THE RIGHT

PROBLEM

PLAYER.

You're not here to have a title. You're here because designing commerce experiences at Nike's scale is one of the hardest design problems on the planet, and that sounds like exactly what you want to work on.

Experience 5+ years product design, 2+ in commerce or marketplace

Portfolio Shipped consumer products at scale (millions of users)

Strength Systems thinking + high visual craft, not one without the other

Bonus You play, run, train, compete. Any sport. Any level.

05 The Offer

MORE THAN

A JOB.

Nike's total rewards are built on the premise that an athlete needs to be whole to perform. That means rest, recovery, flexibility — not just salary.

Base Salary $135,000 – $175,000 depending on level

Equity RSUs vested over 4 years

Product Bonus Annual performance bonus, target 15%

Benefits Medical, dental, vision + Nike product discount

Time Off Flexible PTO + Nike shutdown weeks (winter, summer)

Location Beaverton World HQ — hybrid, 3 days on-site expected

The Creative Agency is a full-service marketing and advertising firm based in Fort Collins. We operate as an external in-house marketing department, bringing strategy, brand, design, digital, media, content, public relations, photography, and video together under one roof.


Our clients span beauty, hospitality, professional services, theatre, public-sector organizations, home services, retail, and B2B industries. The work is varied, fast-moving, and highly visible.


We are not a high-volume design shop built around templates and quick production. Our work is expected to be strategic, distinctive, polished, and strong enough to command attention.


ABOUT THE ROLE


The Creative Agency is seeking an accomplished, hands-on Principal Brand Designer to own the execution and visual quality of brand identities, campaigns, digital experiences, publications, presentations, and marketing materials across our client portfolio.


The right person understands how strategy becomes a visual system and how that system should extend consistently across every brand touchpoint.


Original illustration is required. The Principal Brand Designer must create custom artwork, patterns, motifs, icons, graphic elements, editorial illustrations, and campaign visuals that give a brand distinction. We are not looking for someone whose process depends heavily on stock artwork, purchased elements, generic templates, or whatever design trend happened to wander across TikTok that morning.


This is a highly hands-on position. The Principal Brand Designer will personally concept, design, illustrate, refine, prepare, and complete client work while providing thoughtful creative guidance to developing designers.


The role reports operationally to the Operations Manager and works closely with the CEO and Principal Strategist on brand strategy, campaign direction, and executive creative standards.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About PactFi

Private asset markets (PE, Private Credit, VC, Real Estate) have 10x to 9.8T in AUM over the past decade and are projected to grow to $17T in the next five years. However, digital infrastructure has not kept pace, with most of the market operating predominantly in error-prone, internal-only software solutions.

PactFi provides secure, end-to-end, operational infrastructure for managing complex private credit transactions. Our web-based application brings together all parties involved in such a transaction to more efficiently allocate capital, complete KYC, share documents, manage funds flow, and more. The platform is secured to a bank-grade standard, and we have received our SOC 2 Type 2 attestation.

PactFi was developed in close partnership with two of the industry's largest players, both of whom represent the top 3 players in the private credit space by both size (AUM) and deal activity.

The Design Problem



- Product is moving from a screen-first build model, where the underlying system is designed first and the interface follows. 
- Today's product is fully deterministic, human-driven screens. You'd help define, from scratch, what this platform looks like as AI becomes a first-class part of it — AI agents as a new type of participant alongside human users, and AI as a new interaction modality for human users themselves. 
- Workflows are tied to assets that can live 5–7 years, resurfacing repeatedly at different cadences over that lifetime, with multiple parties holding different views and permissions each time. 
- Clients regularly bring new deal and asset structures the platform hasn't seen before, so the product has to accommodate structural variation it can't fully anticipate. 
- Permissioning is layered — participants often have their own downstream stakeholders who need visibility into a subset of the same information. 
- A point of view on how AI is reshaping what a "product" is — where a great interface is still needed versus where the underlying data itself, exposed well, is becoming the product — is a plus. 

What You'll Do



- Own one or two major product surfaces end-to-end — from problem framing through shipped, polished detail. 
- Design and ship the platform's first real AI-native interaction pattern in an otherwise fully deterministic product — no existing pattern to extend from. 
- Design for dense, structured financial data at scale, and for multi-party, long-running workflows with layered permissions. 
- Work closely with the PM and engineers on your surface to develop the strategy and rationale behind what you build, not just execute a spec. 
- Contribute to and help shape a design system built for extensibility across evolving workflows and asset structures. 
- Set an example in critique and day-to-day work for how design is done here — the work itself is the signal, not a title or mandate.

title: Founding Product Designer
description:
Our client is a financial technology platform built for franchise and independent brand operators.

They serve a massive, underserved economy — 850,000 doors, a $4 trillion market, billions in annual spend, billions in debt originations, and billions spent every year on accounting services alone. Their platform combines expansion loans, an industry-leading charge card, and an AI-powered bookkeeping product into one integrated financial operating system.

They're an engineering and product-driven team, small and fast-moving, working on hard problems with real economic scale behind them.

Role Description

You'll design across our client's full platform — loans, cards, and the AI bookkeeper — with the bookkeeper as the center of gravity. This is a system that will sometimes be wrong, and part of the design challenge is building a front end that handles that honestly: surfacing uncertainty, inviting the user to correct us, and getting smarter because they did. Beyond the correction loop, you're designing how we communicate value — showing people, clearly and concretely, how much time and effort our product is saving them and their business.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

What you'll do:

- Invent interaction paradigms for things that haven't existed before and moke those new paradigms legible and fun

- You've spent the last decade designing software people love to use.
- You're comfortable moving between interaction design, visual design, and product thinking.

We're Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding.

Our mission is simple: double the world's healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

If you don't choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself then, choose the challenge, choose Heidi.

The role

We're looking for a product designer who designs, prototypes, and ships — and knows the difference between software that works and software that makes someone smile.

Clinicians use Heidi to get away from keyboards and back to patients. We want the product to feel as considered as the best software you've ever used — cohesive, quiet, and precise across every surface. When a clinician's tools feel right, they spend less time fighting software and more time with patients. That's the job.
